MINUTES OF 
THE METROPOLITAN BUILDING COMMITTEE

12:30 P.M.

MINUTES: The minutes of the meeting of April 2th having been circulated by mail. 


were taken as read and approved. 


VDERPINNING DRUMMOND ST. BUILDING: Mr. H. M. Patterson reported on the results of 
“an extensive investigation into the condition of the wooden piles under the 
Drummond St. Building. 

In 1947 the Southwest corner of the Building was ‘underpinned. The 
wall adjacent to the University building was examined carefully at the time of 
construction , 1955, and necessary corrections made. The result of recent exam- 
inations revealed the following conditions: 

1, The West wall, south of the Main Entrance, shows no change since being under- 
pinned, The levels of top of band course may not all have been taken at 
exactly the same spot on the moulding as at the prévious date, and thus may 
Vary slightly. North of the Entrance there appears to be very little subsi- 
dence. 


2. The North wall shows little settlement at the West end but this increases as 
it approaches the Budge Hall Mntrance, reaching a maximum of 7/8". 


3. The North wall to the east shows only slight settlement. The north row of 
columns in the Hall are a little lower than those at the south side but sec 
to have subsided almost the same amount as has the wall. 


h, The settlement of the second row of columns from Drummond Street is confirmed. 
(Col. Nos. 5, 6, 7 & 8). The breaking of the paper strips on the third floor 
partitions at Column Nos. 1,2, 3, and indicate that this movement is contin- 
uing. 


5. The settlement at G.3 is also confirmed. The slope of the floor at the doors 
here is very apparent. 


6. The levels around the ppol gallery are all much the same and do not indicate 
seiitlement. There is an old crack in the tile floor between cols. 18 and 19 
which was probably caused by a slight settlement of Columns 1); and 15. The 
fact that the pool footings are at a much lower level than other footings 
would seem to indicate that the water table has remained sufficiently _igh to 
keep these piles constantly wet and that they therefore have not deteriorated. 


7, The settlement of the Basement area under the Gymnasium is also confirmed. 
There are a large number of bad cracks in the partitions in this area, modt 
of which were built about 1955, which indicates comparitively recent movement. 
The floor in this area also shows signs of settlement, probably due to drying 
out of the clgg sub-soil beneath. 


-~2<- 


8, The central area of the Gymnasium is confirmed as being much lower than the 
Side walls. 


The low reading in the south-west corner is due to settlement prior to the 
underpinning when the Sir George Williams Building was built. There were bad 
cracks in the wall at that time, but no settlement should have taken place 
since. 


Based pn these observations the architects recommend underpinning 
14 columns. If at a future date the rest of the building required attention the 
cost is estimated to be $420,000 less possible reduction of those columns around 
the pool because of the low level, leaving a net figure of $35,000. 


Tenders for the immediate job relating to excavation to the under- 
side of 1) pile caps and jacking down new pipe or concrete piles to rock or refu- 
sal and restoring building areas at the point of access were reviewed as follows: 


Foundation Company $83,500. 
J. L. E. Price & Co. Ltd. $52,950. This price is based on a sub-bid 
of the Parco Company for the pile work. 


After considering the matter carefully it was agreed on motion by 
R. E. Heartz, seconded by F. F. Fulton to recommend commencement at once of the 
underpinning by Messrs. J. L. Ik. Price Co. Ltd. at a guaranteed upset price 
including fixed fee of $52,950. It is estimated that the job can be completed by 
Oct. 1, 1963 and that it can be laid out so that all the affected areas will not 
be out of use at the same time. 


The Committee confirmed the suggestion of the Architects that the 
elevations be checked semi-annually. 


CRITICAL PATH SCHEDULING: It was reported that this matter wap being followed. The 
architects have a staff of )O people at work on detailed plans and drawings of the 
S.G.W.U. Building. 


CONTRACT FOR S.G.W.U. BUILDING PROJECT: Further to the review of this subject at 
the last meeting, Messrs. Tait and Sargent have been making further investigations. 
Mr. Tait reported on the favourable comments he ‘had received from the Executive 
officer of the Standard Life Assurance Co. where the project had been placed in 
the hands of a General Contractor and carried out with the Architects, General 
Contractor and the Owner working as a team. Mr. Sargent referred to the method 
to be followed in relation to Place Victoria which is essentially the plan being 
suggested by the Architects. 


After a full discussion of the subject in which both advantages and 
disadvantages were again reviewed, it was agreed on motion by R. &. Heartz, secon- 
ded by W. D. Robb that the Contractors whose names appear below be invited to 
prepare proposals with estimates and a fixed fee. It was understood that any de- 
cision, made on the basis of submissions, would be related to the totality of the 
proposals and not necessarily to the estimates or the fee. It was also agreed that 
draft copies of the proposal invitations be circulated to the members of the 
Committee before dispatch to the contractors listed below: 


E. G. M. Cape & Co., 898 Western Ave. 

J. L. &. Price Co. Ltd. 466 St. Catherine St. West 
Foundation Company of Canada Limited, 1900 Sherbrooke St. West 
Piggott Construction Co. Ltd., 1155 Dorchester Blvd. West 
Pentagon Construction Co. Ltd., 5005 Jean Talon St. West. 


— 


Some discussion took place about the need to include a 


French 


Contractor but there was not sufficient information available about the capacity 


of any such contractor to undertake a project of this dimension.

ARCHITECTS PROPOSAL OF FES: A proposal of the Architects regarding payment of fees 
to be reported for information was tabled because of time. It is as follows: 


"As you know we are now well into the preparation of working drawings and we 
feel we should keep you advised as to our probable drawings aginst fees for the 
next few months. 


Basic Fee 5.3% on $15,000,000.00 = $795,000.00 
Completion of Working Yrawings

15th, which would include billings from May 3lst to Decem- 
ber 1st, or seven months. 
We would suggest a monthly draw of about $33,000.00
